issues.expected: The collision-avoidance sub-machine is reachable from the model root so that its required activation behavior can execute.
issues.observed: Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode is not reached from a top-level initial entry; root reachability contains only the model root and UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.reason: The required collision-avoidance composite is exact and is the target scope of all three activation alternatives, but finite reachability facts show it is not reachable from any top-level initial entry. issues.basis: NL3 scope semantics; NL2 activation transitions; event-consumer facts for collision_detected; finite reachability facts; exact consumer transition refs transition:line:12, transition:line:14, and transition:line:16; closed scope ref state:Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode:line:5.
issues.expected: At least one collision_detected consumer in the active collision-avoidance mode is reachable from the model root, supporting the required activation behavior.
issues.observed: collision_detected has declared consumers transition:line:12, transition:line:14, and transition:line:16, while reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty.
issues.reason: The closed model declares collision_detected consumers on the three owner-local initial transitions, but deterministic event-consumer facts report no reachable consumer from a top-level initial entry. This is an operational coverage gap distinct from declaration and from the separate root-reachability defect.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The event has three declared consumers, and each consumer targets one of the three authored child states; however, deterministic reachability shows none is operationally reachable from the top-level initial path.
issues.title: Collision-detection consumers are declared but unreachable

issues.basis: NL3; canonical concurrent hierarchy and four source region projections; closed-model composite and region projections; absence of finite trace or SMT evidence for concurrent activation semantics; exact scope binding to Collision_Avoidance_Active_Mode.
issues.expected: Different collision-avoidance controls can be active concurrently within the active collision-avoidance mode.
issues.observed: The supplied facts establish orthogonal region structure and child states, but do not establish a runtime concurrent-activation trace or a frozen predicate for this behavior-occurrence property.
issues.reason: The source and closed model establish four orthogonal region projections under the active collision-avoidance composite, but the atomic behavior-occurrence contract requires concurrent activation semantics that no supplied finite trace, verify fact, or frozen predicate directly expresses. The precise semantic obligation is therefore retained as an unsupported candidate rather than replaced by region existence.
issues.requirement_quote: allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The explicit orthogonal region projections are structural evidence supporting possible concurrency, but they do not by themselves prove the required runtime activation behavior.
issues.title: Concurrent activation semantics are unsupported by the frozen registry
